scenes.title: Empty state / Load Demo Phantom
scenes.text: This is CT Beam Studio. Load the demo phantom.

scenes.title: 2D slices and 3D gantry side by side
scenes.text: No patient data needed, it runs a Shepp-Logan phantom. Axial and coronal slices on the left, and the gantry in 3D on the right.

scenes.title: 3D geometry and legend overlays
scenes.text: The 3D view draws the projection geometry: source trajectory, detector, isocenter, and central beam. Legend entries toggle each overlay, one at a time.

scenes.title: Sinogram Inspection tab
scenes.text: Sinogram Inspection puts measured data side by side, with what this volume would produce.

scenes.title: Sample options and beam energy
scenes.text: Sample options restrict the run to a few projections, rows, or columns, of the selected geometry and detector size. Beam energy sets the Hounsfield-to-attenuation conversion.

scenes.title: Run Forward Projection and the wait
scenes.spoken: Run Forward Projection traces rays through the volume with parallel proj. With a GPU when CUDA is available, otherwise on the CPU. One simulated projection per gantry angle, sixty in this case.
scenes.text: Run Forward Projection traces rays through the volume with parallelproj. With a GPU when CUDA is available, otherwise on the CPU. One simulated projection per gantry angle, sixty in this case.

scenes.title: Measured vs simulated, metrics per slice
scenes.text: Results: measured, simulated, and the difference, scored per slice with mean absolute error, RMSE, and SSIM.

scenes.title: Curves, distributions, projection scrub
scenes.text: Curves and distributions show where the two disagree. Scrub the index, to inspect a single view, then read its scores. That comparison, checking scanner geometry against real acquisitions, is the point of the tool.
